{{Elections in Virginia}}
The '''2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Virginia''' were held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[U.S. representative]]s from the [[U.S.]] Commonwealth of [[Virginia]], one from each of the state's eleven [[Virginia's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections coincided with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various [[2024 United States elections|state and local elections]]. The primary elections took place on June 18, 2024.

{{see also|Virginia's 1st congressional district}}
The 1st district is based in the western [[Chesapeake Bay]] and includes portions of suburban [[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond]]. Within the district are western [[Henrico County, Virginia|Henrico]] and [[Chesterfield County, Virginia|Chesterfield]] counties. Other localities in the district include [[Colonial Beach, Virginia|Colonial Beach]], [[Mechanicsville, Virginia|Mechanicsville]], and [[Williamsburg, Virginia|Williamsburg]]. The incumbent was Republican [[Rob Wittman]], who was reelected with 56.02% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT">{{cite web|url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/charts/house-charts/national-house-vote-tracker/2022|title=2022 National House Vote Tracker|access-date=January 8, 2024|website=[[The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter|Cook Political Report]]}}</ref>

{{see also|Virginia's 2nd congressional district}}
The 2nd district is based in [[Hampton Roads]], containing the cities of [[Chesapeake, Virginia|Chesapeake]], [[Franklin, Virginia|Franklin]], [[Suffolk, Virginia|Suffolk]], and [[Virginia Beach, Virginia|Virginia Beach]]. Virginia's [[Eastern Shore of Virginia|Eastern Shore]] is also located within the district. The incumbent was Republican [[Jen Kiggans]], who flipped the district and was elected to a first term with 52% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/> She won re-election, defeating Democrat Missy Cotter Smasal 51%–47%.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 6, 2024 |title=AP Race Call: Republican Jen Kiggans wins reelection to U.S. House in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District |url=http://www.wavy.com/news/politics/ap-ap-race-call-republican-jen-kiggans-wins-reelection-to-u-s-house-in-virginias-2nd-congressional-district/ | work=Wavy}}</ref>

{{see also|Virginia's 4th congressional district}}
The 4th district takes in the city of [[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond]] and portions of [[Southside (Virginia)|Southside Virginia]] following [[Interstate 95 in Virginia|Interstate 95]]. Within the district are the cities of [[Colonial Heights, Virginia|Colonial Heights]], [[Emporia, Virginia|Emporia]], [[Hopewell, Virginia|Hopewell]], and [[Petersburg, Virginia|Petersburg]]. The incumbent was Democrat [[Jennifer McClellan]], who was elected with 74.41% of the vote in a [[2023 Virginia's 4th congressional district special election|2023 special election]] after the previous incumbent, [[Donald McEachin]], died.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 February Special |url=https://results.elections.virginia.gov/vaelections/2023%20February%20Special/Site/Congress.html |access-date=January 8, 2024 |date=March 1, 2023 |website=Virginia Department of Elections}}</ref>

{{see also|Virginia's 5th congressional district}}
The 5th district encompasses the majority of [[Southside (Virginia)|Southside Virginia]], including the cities of [[Charlottesville, Virginia|Charlottesville]], [[Danville, Virginia|Danville]], and [[Lynchburg, Virginia|Lynchburg]]. The incumbent was Republican [[Bob Good]], who was reelected with 57.68% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/>

===Republican primary===
Good was considered to be vulnerable in his primary, as he had received criticism for being one of eight Republicans who [[Removal of Kevin McCarthy as Speaker of the House|voted to oust]] [[Kevin McCarthy]] as [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|speaker of the House]]. He also faced backlash from [[Donald Trump]] and his supporters for endorsing [[Ron DeSantis]] in the [[2024 Republican presidential primaries]].<ref name=":0" />

{{see also|Virginia's 6th congressional district}}
The 6th district is located in western Virginia taking in the [[Shenandoah Valley]] along [[Interstate 81]]. The district is anchored at the southern end by the cities of [[Roanoke, Virginia|Roanoke]] and [[Salem, Virginia|Salem]]. The incumbent was Republican [[Ben Cline]], who was re-elected with 64.50% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/>

{{see also|Virginia's 7th congressional district}}
The 7th district is based in [[Northern Virginia]] and encompasses suburban and exurban areas of [[Washington, D.C.|Washington]], as well as rural areas of the Piedmont. The district contains  [[Bowling Green, Virginia|Bowling Green]], [[Culpeper, Virginia|Culpeper]], the city of [[Fredericksburg, Virginia|Fredericksburg]], [[Stafford, Virginia|Stafford]], [[Stanardsville, Virginia|Stanardsville]], [[Woodbridge, Virginia|Woodbridge]], and a small sliver of [[Albemarle County, Virginia|Albemarle County]]. The incumbent was Democrat [[Abigail Spanberger]], who was re-elected with 52.33% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/> Spanberger did not seek re-election, but would instead run for governor in [[2025 Virginia gubernatorial election|2025]].<ref name = SpanGov/> Anderson was dogged through the campaign by B-roll footage he had shot with the wife and children of a family friend, giving the false impression that he was married with children, and leading to accusations that he was misleading voters with a "fake family".<ref name="m288">{{cite web | last=Karni | first=Annie | last2=Edmondson | first2=Catie | title=G.O.P. Candidates, Looking to Soften Their Image, Turn to Their Wives | website=The New York Times | date=2024-09-27 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/27/us/politics/republican-candidates-wives-ads.html | access-date=2024-12-28}}</ref><ref name="n582">{{cite web | last=Armus | first=Teo | title=A ‘fake family’ photo takes center stage in battleground House race | website=Washington Post | date=2024-10-28 | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2024/10/28/derrick-anderson-congress-virginia-7th-district-vindman/ | access-date=2024-12-28}}</ref> Vindman ultimately won the election by 10,489 votes.

The 8th district is based in [[northern Virginia]] and encompasses the inner [[Washington, D.C.]] suburbs, including [[Arlington County, Virginia|Arlington]], [[Alexandria, Virginia|Alexandria]], and [[Falls Church, Virginia|Falls Church]]. The incumbent was Democrat [[Don Beyer]], who was re-elected with 73.67% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/>

{{see also|Virginia's 10th congressional district}}
The 10th district is based in northern Virginia and the D.C. metro area, encompassing [[Fauquier County, Virginia|Fauquier]], [[Loudoun County, Virginia|Loudoun]], and [[Rappahannock County, Virginia|Rappahannock]] counties, the independent cities of [[Manassas, Virginia|Manassas]] and [[Manassas Park, Virginia|Manassas Park]], and portions of [[Fairfax County, Virginia|Fairfax]] and [[Prince William County, Virginia|Prince William]] counties. The incumbent was Democrat [[Jennifer Wexton]], who was re-elected with 53.26% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/> Wexton announced that she would not seek re-election in 2024, citing a diagnosis of [[progressive supranuclear palsy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Herb |date=2023-09-18 |title=Citing health issues, Wexton decides not to run again |url=https://rollcall.com/2023/09/18/citing-health-issues-wexton-decides-not-to-run-again/ |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Roll Call |language=en-US}}</ref>

{{see also|Virginia's 11th congressional district}}
The 11th district encompasses portions of suburban [[Washington, D.C.]], including the city of [[Fairfax, Virginia|Fairfax]] and portions of [[Fairfax County, Virginia|Fairfax County]]. The incumbent was Democrat [[Gerry Connolly]], who was re-elected with 66.89% of the vote in 2022.<ref name="HPVT"/>
